aula.objetivo: Form the instrumental in the singular and plural and use it for «with», instruments, professions, seasons of the year and the prepositions of place.

blocos.texto: (or: the case of the body's extensions — and the difference between the “with” of instrument and the “with” of company)

blocos.titulo: The instrumental: the "extension of the body"
blocos.explicacao: Picture a scene you will probably live. You are in Russia and you want to say that you write with a pen. You think: "pen in Russian is ру́чка, and 'with' is с, so I will say я пишу́ с ру́чкой." The person gives you a puzzled look and corrects you: — Я пишу́ ру́чкой. You stare. It is the same word, ру́чка, but now it is in the instrumental (ру́чкой) and you did not use с. You wonder: "But I wanted to say with the pen! Why no с?" And the person explains: — Because the pen does not go along with you. The pen is part of you when you write. The pen is the extension of your hand. That is the doorway into the instrumental case, and it shows a beauty that English hides. Pay attention: after this lesson you will understand one of the biggest differences between the two languages. The little secret: the extension of the body. In English, the word "with" has two completely different senses that we never notice. Sense 1, instrument (the thing is an extension of your body): I write with a pen. I eat soup with a spoon. I cut bread with a knife. I paint with a brush. Sense 2, company (the thing is another person, not an extension): I go with you. I live with my mother. I talk with the teacher. I work with my colleagues. English uses the same word "with" for both, automatically. Nobody thinks about it. In Russian this is impossible: the two "with" are different structures. Sense 1 (instrument) = the bare instrumental, with no preposition. Sense 2 (company) = С + instrumental. See for yourself. Notice: in the first case the pen and the spoon are extensions of the body. You write, and the pen is part of the movement of your hand. You eat, and the spoon is part of the movement of your hand. The thing does not go with you; at that moment it is you. In the second case you and the other person are two separate beings. You go, and they go. You live, and they live. That is company, so it needs с.

tabelas.titulo: The little secret: the extension of the body

linhas.ENGLISH: I eat soup with a spoon.

blocos.explicacao: The painter metaphor. Here is a metaphor worth the whole lesson. Imagine Da Vinci without a brush. How would he paint the Mona Lisa? He would not. The brush is an extension of his hand. Without it his hand cannot do the action of painting. The brush is part of Da Vinci at the moment of painting. In Russian, Da Vinci painted ки́стью (a brush: bare instrumental), not с ки́стью, because the brush was not a companion. It was an extension of his hand. Another example: you eat soup. Without a spoon you cannot eat soup (unless you lift the bowl, but that is another matter). The spoon is the extension of your hand at the moment of eating. So in Russian you eat soup ло́жкой (bare instrumental), not с ло́жкой. Third example: you write a letter. Without a pen you cannot write. The pen is the extension of your hand at the moment of writing. So you write ру́чкой, not с ру́чкой. Now compare with company: you go to the cinema. You go, and your friend goes. Your friend is not an extension of your body. Your friend is another person, with their own will, their own feet, their own path. So you go с дру́гом (with the friend: С + instrumental). That is all. The rule is one question: is the thing an extension of your body? YES = bare instrumental (ру́чкой, ло́жкой, ки́стью). NO (it is another person or an independent thing) = С + instrumental (с дру́гом, с ма́мой). The magic question solves about 90% of cases. Here is how you decide between the bare instrumental and С + instrumental.

tabelas.titulo: The magic question: is the thing an extension of the body?

linhas.SENTENCE: I eat soup with a spoon.
I cut the bread with a knife.

blocos.explicacao: The 6 prepositions of the instrumental. The instrumental is governed by 6 main prepositions: «с» (company) and five that express position. All of them express an idea of position or relation. One big rule: the change always comes AFTER the preposition. The preposition itself never changes; it is fixed. What changes is the word that follows it: the noun goes into the instrumental. Look at the examples. Notice that the preposition (над, под, пе́ред, ме́жду, за, с) is always the same, and it is the noun that takes the instrumental ending. That is why we say the preposition "governs" the instrumental: it demands that the word after it be in that case.

linhas.EXAMPLE: пе́ред до́мом (in front of the house)
ме́жду столо́м и дива́ном (between the table and the sofa)

linhas.PREPOSITION + NOUN: ме́жду + стол и диван → ме́жду столо́м и дива́ном
linhas.O QUE MUDOU: стол turned into столо́м, диван turned into дива́ном

blocos.explicacao: The instrumental answers «кем? чем?». In English we use "with" and "by means of". Singular: hard masculine: -ом (брат → братом); soft masculine (-й, -ь): -ем (учитель → учителем, музей → музеем). After ж, ч, ш, щ and ц: -ем if the ending is unstressed (муж → мужем) and -ом if it is stressed (врач → врачом). Feminine: -а → -ой (мама → мамой); -я → -ей (неделя → неделей); -ь → -ью (ночь → ночью, дочь → дочерью). Neuter: -о → -ом (окно → окном); -е → -ем (море → морем). Plural, all genders: -ами or -ями (книги → книгами, студенты → студентами). Irregular: друзья → друзьями, дети → детьми, люди → людьми.
blocos.comparacao: in English "with my brother" does not change the word "brother". In Russian the noun itself changes: «с братом».

tabelas.titulo: Pronouns (after «с» the 3rd person gets an н-)

erros.motivo: The pronoun goes into the instrumental: с ним.

blocos.enunciado: Say: «Я работаю с братом. Я говорю с другом. Я ем ложкой.»
Write the instrumental of 5 words and the instrumental pronouns.
